title: Screen reading trails paper for information
statement: Expect comprehension of on-screen informational text to trail paper, more under time pressure, so keep time pressure off on-screen reading and ask for a self-check before showing answers.
example: A meta-analysis of 54 studies found paper beat screen by an effect size of 0.21, with the gap only for expository text.
detail: The Grade 9 desktop design brief cites two meta-analyses. Across 54 studies paper beat screen (g = −0.21), the gap appearing only for expository text and growing under time pressure, with no advantage for digital natives; across 33 studies the gap was g = −0.25 overall, −0.32 for expository text and −0.04 for narrative, and screen readers judged their own understanding less accurately. The brief's implication is to assume informational texts suffer most on screen, remove time pressure and ask for a self-check before showing answers.
against: The second meta-analysis was read from its indexed abstract after the fetch failed (`othello-course-renderer-draft/repo/docs/design/grade-9/research/edtech-desktop-design.md`, line 186), and for narrative text the gap was close to zero (−0.04).

evidence.quote: Delgado et al. (2018) meta-analysis, 54 studies: paper beats screen, g = −0.21.
The gap appears only for expository text, grows under time pressure, and digital natives show no advantage.
Clinton (2019), 33 studies: g = −0.25 overall, −0.32 for expository text, −0.04 for narrative.
Screen readers also judged their own understanding less accurately.
